newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: More talks needed to form Slovenia govt - Kucan.
newsitem.headline: More talks needed to form Slovenia govt - Kucan.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan said on Wednesday he would hold a second round of talks with party leaders to try to break a deadlock over forming a new coalition government.
"So far, the positions of the parties do not give majority support to any one candidate," Kucan told a news conference.

Kucan, who held initial talks this week, said political parties were divided between supporting Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek of the centre-left Liberal Democrats and the conservative People's Party, headed by Marjan Podobnik.
"It is in the interest of the state that we get a new and stable government as soon as possible," Kucan said.
The Liberal Democrats won the most votes in Slovenia's November 10 general election, capturing 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats.
The People's Party is the biggest of three right-wing parties in an alliance called the "Slovenian Spring", which won 45 seats in parliament, just one short of an absolute majority.
Kucan did not specify when the formal second round of talks would begin, and said unofficial talks between the parties would carry on.
Under the constitution, Kucan must name a candidate to form a government by January 3.
